counterclim_tropical_cyclones.title: Tropical cyclone tracks and windfields
counterclim_tropical_cyclones.comment: We do not provide "no climate change" TC tracks and windfields but the original tracks from the IBTrACS database ([Knapp et al. 2010](https://doi.org/10.1175/2009BAMS2755.1)) (period 1841-2021) windfields calculated by Holland model ([Holland 1980](https://doi.org/10.1175/1520-0493(1980)108%3C1212:AAMOTW%3E2.0.CO;2), [Holland 2008](https://doi.org/10.1175/2008MWR2395.1)) should be used in combination with the counterfactual water levels to estimate the impacts of sea level rise on TC induced damages, losses or replacement.

counterclim_lightning.title: Lightning
counterclim_lightning.comment: We do not provide "no climate change" lightning data. Instead the original Flash Rate Monthly Climatology from [Cecil (2006)](https://doi.org/10.5067/LIS/LIS-OTD/DATA303) should be used in the **counterclim** set-up.

counterclim_ocean.title: Oceanic forcing data

histsoc.description: **Varying direct human influences** in the historical period.
histsoc.description_note: Please label your model run `histsoc` **even if** it only partly accounts for varying direct human forcings while another part of the the direct human forcing is considered constant or is ignored.

1901soc.description: **Fixed year-1901 direct human influences** (e.g. land use, nitrogen deposition and fertilizer input, fishing effort).
1901soc.description_note: Please only label your simulations `1901soc` if they do not at all account for historical changes in direct human forcing, but they do represent constant year-1901 levels of direct human forcing for at least some direct human forcings. This scenario may be thought of an approximation of pre-industrial levels of human impacts.

2021soc.description: **Fixed year-2021 direct human influences** (e.g. land use, nitrogen deposition and fertilizer input, fishing effort).
2021soc.description_note: Please label your simulations `2021soc` if they do not at all account for historical changes in direct human forcing, but they do represent constant year-2021 levels of direct human forcing for at least some direct human forcings.

2021soc-from-histsoc.description: **Fixed year-2021 direct human influences** (e.g. land use, nitrogen deposition and fertilizer input, fishing effort) for the future period, if the historical period was using varying direct human influences in the historical period.
2021soc-from-histsoc.description_note: Please label your simulations `2021soc-from-histsoc` for the future period, if your model run extends a historical period which used the `histsoc` scenario. This distinguishes the data from experiments which use both `2021soc` in the past and the future. If your model output is identical for both cases, please only submit the `2021soc` files for the future period.

ssp1vlsoc-noadapt.description: Varying direct human influences in the future period according to the **very low emission scenario**, not accounting for the impact of climate change under the corresponding climate.

ssp1vlsoc-adapt.description: Varying direct human influences in the future period according to the **very low emission scenario**, accounting for the impact of climate change under the corresponding climate.
ssp1vlsoc-adapt.description_note: **This experiment is not part of the ISIMIP4b Fast Track.**

nbp.long_name: Carbon Mass Flux out of Atmosphere due to Net Biospheric Production on Land

fluc.long_name: Carbon Mass Flux into Atmosphere from Land Use Change
fluc.comment: For wood products only. Sum of carbon fluxes to wood production and wood storage turnover emissions from previous years.

fgrazing.long_name: Carbon Mass Flux into Atmosphere from Grazing

fcropharvest.long_name: Carbon Mass Flux into Atmosphere from Crop Harvesting

flittersoil.long_name: Total Carbon Flux from Litter to Soil

flittersoillayer.comment: If possible, provide carbon fluxes for all depth layers (i.e. 3D-field), and indicate depth in m. Otherwise, only provide “flittersoil-total. See instructions for depth layers on <https://www.isimip.org/protocol/preparing-simulation-files>.

fvegsoil.long_name: Total Carbon Flux from Vegetation Directly to Soil

fvegsoillayer.long_name: Total Carbon Mass Flux from Vegetation Directly to Soil in each layer
fvegsoillayer.comment: If possible, provide carbon fluxes for all depth layers (i.e. 3D-field), and indicate depth in m. Otherwise, only provide “fvegsoil-total. See instructions for depth layers on <https://www.isimip.org/protocol/preparing-simulation-files>.

wetlandch4.long_name: Grid averaged methane emissions from wetland

ch4.long_name: Total Surface Carbon Mass Flux into CH4 emissions

rsoillayer.long_name: Carbon Mass Flux into Atmosphere due to Soil Respiration on Land of pools with different turnover time in each layer
rsoillayer.comment: If possible, provide soil respiration for all depth layers (i.e. 3D-field), and indicate depth in m. If you do not report layers, the depth dimension is 1. rsoil.long_name: Carbon Mass Flux into Atmosphere due to Soil Respiration on Land

verticalcflux.long_name: Vertical Carbon Mass Flux between layers

rlitter.long_name: Carbon Mass Flux into Atmosphere due to Litter Respiration on Land in each layer

rhlayer.long_name: Carbon Mass Flux into Atmosphere due to Heterotrophic Respiration on Land in each layer

absdom.comment: Same as abs but split into different sectors if available.

absind.comment: Same as abs but split into different sectors if available.

absliv.comment: Same as abs but split into different sectors if available.

lfrf.comment: Cell-by-cell flow (right). Leaving the cell = negative values; entering the cell = positive values.

lfff.comment: Cell-by-cell flow (front). Leaving the cell = negative values; entering the cell = positive values.

lflf.comment: Cell-by-cell flow (lower) when more than 1 groundwater layer is simulated. Leaving the cell = negative values; entering the cell = positive values.

default.title: Default
default.description: Model should use their individual “best representation” of the historical period with regard to sowing dates, harvesting dates, fertilizer application rates and crop varieties.

fullharm.title: Fully harmonized
fullharm.description: Simulations based on prescribed “present day” fertilization rates (available for download) and fixed planting and harvesting dates (also available for download). Modelers should have planting as closely as possible to these dates, but it may be admissible to use these dates as indicators for planting windows (depending on model specifics).

harmnon.title: Harmonized seasons with no N constraints
harmnon.description: For models with an explicit description of the nitrogen cycle: harmnon simulations should be run with nitrogen stress turned off completely or (if that’s not possible) with very high N application rates to make model results comparable between those GGCMs that have explicit N dynamics and those that do not. For models without the nitrogen cycle: harmnon and fullharm simulations are the same and do not need to be duplicated. Please contact the sector coordination to push on with this side branch.
